source.title: UniWAM: Unified World-Action Model
source.authors: Wenxuan Song; Jiayi Chen; Jingbo Wang; Shuai Zhou; Xicheng Gong; Zehua Fan; Ziyang Zhou; Junwu E; Haodong Yan; Fuhao Li; Qize Yu; Xu Huang; Pengwei Wang; Wen Chen; Shunbo Zhou; Haoang Li

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figure text is garbled, but the scaling results needed here are also stated in the prose and equation.
record.tranche_reason: Extends scaling-law evidence to robot and human-robot embodied pretraining, measuring validation loss against data hours and downstream manipulation performance against data scale.
record.gate_note: The study does not test language-model loss scaling with parameter count, tokens, or training compute, or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation. Its relevant results concern UniWAM validation loss versus embodied pretraining data hours and downstream OOD manipulation performance versus data scale.
record.test_reason: The study pretrains one robot world-action model (UniWAM) on 250 to 5k hours of robot data, with or without matched human egocentric data. It reports converged validation loss and downstream OOD success against data scale. This is a new setting (embodied pretraining, data-only scaling) with its own results on V5 and V6. It does not vary parameters or compute.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report a 'log-linear scaling law' of converged validation loss with data hours. They say OOD success rises with robot data without saturation, and that human data helps only from about 1k hours. They suggest validation loss can serve as an indicator of embodied control capability.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales embodied robot/human data and measures validation loss and manipulation performance, rather than scaling language-model parameters, tokens, or compute and measuring held-out cross-entropy.
record.method_sensitivity: The effect of adding human egocentric data depends on scale: it degrades performance at small scales and yields gains once training data reaches 1k hours.
record.code_released: not stated (the text shows a GitHub link label but no URL)
record.problems: The scaling evidence is for one embodied model and one pretraining setup, not language-model size or compute scaling. The validation-loss fit is reported for data hours only. The text gives no uncertainty estimates, and most intermediate data-scale and downstream-performance values are not stated numerically.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant scaling results left out. Other benchmark and ablation results do not measure the scaling-law outcomes covered by the claim versions tested here.

untested.parts: Language-model cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens or compute is not tested.
No extrapolation from small runs to much larger runs is attempted.
Compute-optimal parameter/data allocation is not studied; model size is fixed.
Architecture shape at fixed parameter count is not varied.
Parameter and compute scaling in the embodied setting is untested, as are other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer laws.
The study does not examine whether its fitted form depends on setup or fitting choices.

missing.what: Separate validation-MSE and success values per data scale for the Robot and Robot+Human curves. Also missing: which points enter the Eq. 10 fit, and whether loss and success diverge across mixtures.

record.verdict_notes: Robotics paper (UniWAM); scaling is a secondary section (5.3). There is a single model size, no uncertainty and no repeated runs. 'Scaling law' here means L = 0.03205 − 0.00302·ln(D), not a Kaplan/Chinchilla-style power law. The source is inconsistent on whether D counts robot-only or robot plus human hours.

versions.untested_parts: Language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether fits from small runs predict losses of much larger runs.
Effects of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
Only validation loss for UniWAM embodied pretraining versus robot/human data hours is examined; other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, and transfer settings are not tested.
Only OOD manipulation performance and its relation to data scale or validation loss are examined; downstream language-model tasks and a quantitative loss-to-task prediction are not tested.
Whether exponents or compute-optimal splits depend on setup or fitting choices, or curves bend away from a single power law.

rows.subject: UniWAM
rows.size_stated: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B backbones; total parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Related converged validation loss to the scale of robot and human pretraining data.

conditions.value: D is hours of robot and human pretraining data
VQA data included in all settings

rows.measure: Validation loss at convergence (Figure 7 identifies the plotted quantity as validation MSE).
rows.note: The authors describe this as a log-linear scaling law over the explored data scales; D is measured in hours.
rows.check: The fitted form is log-linear, L = a − b·ln(D), not a power law. It has no irreducible term and would turn negative at large D. It spans about 1.3 orders of magnitude (250 to 5k robot hours; ~10k with human data) at one model size. The loss is a flow-matching validation MSE, not cross-entropy. The text defines D as robot plus human hours, but the Figure 7 caption says the x-axis is robot hours. Which curve(s) the fit uses, and how many points, is not stated.

rows.subject: UniWAM
rows.size_stated: Qwen3-VL-2B-Instruct and Wan2.2-TI2V-5B backbones; total parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Varied robot pretraining data scale and reported OOD manipulation completion.

conditions.value: VQA data included in all settings

rows.value: Rises monotonically from 0.35 at 250 hours to 0.67 at 5k hours; no signs of saturation in the explored regime.
rows.note: The text also lists tested robot-data scales of 250, 500, 1k, 2.5k, and 5k hours, but does not state each intermediate outcome.
rows.check: The text calls the measure 'average task completion'. The Figure 7 caption calls it RoboTwin clean2rand success rate. Only the endpoints are given; intermediate values are not stated. The setting is a single model size, scaled by data only.

Real-world robot performance and downstream task success

rows.measure: Relationship between validation loss and downstream task success
rows.value: Validation loss decreases alongside improvements in downstream task success; the authors say the offline scaling trend closely tracks real-world robot performance.
rows.note: This is a qualitative correspondence; the text does not provide a quantitative loss-to-performance prediction.
rows.check: A qualitative statement only. No quantitative loss-to-success mapping or correlation is reported.
